newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up as exporters unload dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up as exporters unload dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso gained on Wednesday after exporters started selling their dollars to banks, dealers said.
"Exporters decided to unload their dollars ahead of a further rise in the peso. The strengthening of the peso in recent days encouraged them to do so," a trader said.
Banks with long dollar positions also sold dollars, another trader said.
The peso ended at 28.49 from the previous close of 28.65. Volume was higher at $74.1 million from $25 million.
Traders said the central bank did not intervene in the market but it quoted offer rates for the dollar at 28.80 to 28.60 from a previous 29.
The peso may still rise up to 28.40 on Thursday, a dealer said.
"Below 28.50, many firms would be willing to buy dollars," a trader said.
